note: Dial hints, not authority. An entry here can send you to the wrong machine and cannot make you trust it: a peer id is sha256 of its McEliece transport key, so the handshake decides who answered and this file decides nothing. That is why publishing it on GitHub Pages is safe, and why losing GitHub Pages costs a hint rather than the network. See docs/discovery.md.
key_files: seeds/<transport>.key, relative to this file: the hex transport public key, 522240 characters. The file is named by the sha256 of the bytes it decodes to, so `cairn seeds` checks the name against the content and refuses a mismatch.

seeds.name: tunnel
seeds.note: Replaces us-west at 44.251.117.84, which stopped answering. p2p dials bore.pub:56276; on 2026-10-05 a second node reached that address and the seed handed over the key named here. The port is a bore.pub forward onto the node, and the HTTPS reader in front of the same node is https://auto-controls-healing-player.trycloudflare.com . Neither forward is a leased address: both end when the process behind them stops, and the next process gets a new port and a new tunnel name. The http field stays the GitHub Pages mirror so a browser does not treat an empty fresh log as the published snapshot. That mirror is filled by node-sync from a durable node; until then /node/health is not the text ok and the site keeps the bundled launch log. The handshake still decides who answered.
